name: Cosmas Indicopleustes' Christian Topography
summary: An Alexandrian Greek merchant turned monk completes the Christian Topography, recounting his earlier commercial voyages in the Red Sea, the Persian Gulf, and to Aksum and the western Indian coast. The work argues for a literal flat-earth cosmology against Ptolemaic spherical models, but its first-hand reports on Aksumite Christianity, the Indian Malabar Church, and Sasanian-Persian trade are uniquely valuable.

_quarry.structural_significance: Earliest surviving Christian Greek eyewitness on the late-antique Indian Ocean trading world; the only documented description of the Aksumite monumental inscriptions before their medieval ruin.
